rewrite: A former member of the House Democratic leadership is challenging President Joe Biden's bid for re-election by launching his own campaign for the presidency. Stan Freberg, a legendary comedian who revolutionized the advertising industry with his satirical approach, died of natural causes. Freberg's innovative style inspired countless artists and advertisers, earning him numerous accolades throughout his career. Born in 1931, Freberg started his career as a radio host in Los Angeles before moving into television and film. Over the years, he became known for his hilarious commercial campaigns, music parodies, and witty commentary on popular culture. Freberg's work continues to influence modern-day advertising and entertainment.

Photographer Kate Parker has earned praise for her photo series "Strong is the New Pretty," which shows her two daughters and their friends being typically wild, freckled, muddy children. Most of the photos capture moments of childish wonder and energy rather than posed scenes. The idea for the series began when Parker asked her older daughter to show her bravest face on the eve of her first triathlon. Parker has said that she wants to capture her daughters' sense of self-confidence and help them keep it for as long as possible. She also hopes to inspire parents to find their own creative ways to document their children's lives.

A Polish prince has challenged British politician Nigel Farage to a duel in London's Hyde Park over his immigration policy. Prince Jan Zylinski is upset with discrimination against Poles living in Britain and rejects Farage's claim that migrants are causing traffic jams as nonsense. He wants to settle the matter through a traditional duel with a sword. Farage, however, does not intend to accept the offer and instead proposes a duel with words on a TV show before the general election. Zylinski agrees and proposes a separate video duel. Meanwhile, another UKIP politician tweeted an image of a medieval knight being sliced in two, suggesting that Farage would do the same to the prince.

Naseem Roulack, an escaped inmate from Virginia, was captured after two months on the run. He was taken into custody by the U.S. Marshals Service and Fairfax County Police Department. Roulack had escaped from a hospital where he was being treated, and was implicated in an armed carjacking and kidnapping in Maryland. Two corrections officers were fired for falling asleep on the job, allowing Roulack to escape.

Officer Michael Slager, who is white, fired eight shots at an unarmed black man named Walter Scott while Scott was fleeing on foot. Scott sustained five wounds and died. The shooting has sparked national outrage and protests in the city of North Charleston. The FBI is investigating, and South Carolina lawmakers are examining police body camera legislation. The mayor of North Charleston condemned the shooting at a news conference and announced that the city would add 150 more body cameras for its officers. The video of the shooting has circulated widely on social media and has drawn comparisons to the Michael Brown case in Ferguson, Missouri. Not everyone agrees that the shootings are similar or that race played a factor. The autopsy report stated that Scott died as a result of a homicide, but it did not specify which bullet caused his death. The video shows that Scott attempted to flee the scene, and his family believes he was running for his life. Some witnesses have reported seeing a struggle between the two men before the shooting, but police officials claim that there was no fight.

A federal court has issued a preliminary injunction against a debt collection scheme targeting veterans. Three individuals and two corporations based in Oklahoma ran the scheme, including Christopher Parks, who recently faced an 18-month prison sentence for healthcare fraud. The Department of Defense's Office of Inspector General's Defense Criminal Investigative Service led the investigation, which involved multiple agencies and resulted in the seizure of property and assets related to the scheme.

The release of "Furious 7" on Friday marks the end of Paul Walker's journey in the Fast & Furious franchise. The movie is an emotional tribute to the late actor, who died in November 2013 at the age of 40 after a car crash. Walker's death was particularly eerie given his sudden rise to fame and his role as a former cop turned road racer in the franchise. The movie's script was rewritten, and special effects were used to finish scenes with Walker's brothers, Cody and Caleb, serving as body doubles. The movie premiered on Wednesday night in Hollywood, and Vin Diesel delivered a tearful speech, calling the film more than just a movie. He also revealed that he had named his newborn daughter after Walker. The movie has received multiple tributes leading up to its release, with about 5,000 people attending an outdoor memorial for Walker just a week after his death. The movie is expected to generate over $80 million in its opening weekend.

Authorities in South Carolina have released dash cam footage of the fatal shooting of Walter Scott by North Charleston police officer Michael Slager. The footage shows Slager approaching Scott's vehicle, speaking with him through the window, and then Scott exiting the vehicle and running away. Officer Michael Slager, a five-year veteran of the North Charleston Police Department in South Carolina, has been fired after a video emerged showing him fatally shooting an unarmed black man, Walter Scott, during a traffic stop. Sabeen Mahmud, social advocate and founder of a Karachi-based cafe that served as a hub for social discourse and art, was murdered in a drive-by shooting on Friday. Mahmud's cafe, T2F (The Second Floor), had become a vital space for open discussion, and she had become a figurehead for love, tolerance and humanism. Israelis gathered to honor the country's fallen soldiers and remember victims of terror on Memorial Day. Richard Corliss, a film critic for Time magazine for 35 years, has died at the age of 71. Corliss was known for his appreciation of all movie genres, from arty dramas to epic fantasies. He compiled a top 100 movies list that included films ranging from "Pulp Fiction" to "Finding Nemo" to "Drunken Master II." Corliss freely criticized big movies he found overrated, including "Titanic" and "Star Wars." He also disliked sentimental and uplifting movies that often become mainstream hits and win Oscars. Corliss reviewed over 1,000 movies, authored four books on film, and served as editor of Film Comment for 20 years. He is survived by his wife, Mary, who is also a film critic.

1. Limit purine-rich foods: Consuming less meat, poultry, seafood, and pulses reduces uric acid levels. Vegetables such as cauliflower, asparagus, spinach, peas, and mushrooms are also high in purines and should be consumed in moderation.
2. Increase vitamin C intake: Vitamin C helps to disintegrate uric acid and force it out of the body through urine. Foods rich in vitamin C include lemons, cherries, dark berries, and other citrus fruits.
3. Reduce alcohol consumption: Excessive alcohol consumption contributes to high uric acid levels. Limiting or avoiding alcohol intake helps reduce uric acid levels.
4. Stay hydrated: Drinking plenty of water can help flush out uric acid from the body.
5. Consider supplements: Some supplements such as celery seed extract, turmeric, and ginger have been shown to help reduce uric acid levels. However, consult a healthcare professional before taking any supplements.

These remedies do not work for everyone and do not completely eliminate high uric acid levels. If you have persistently high uric acid levels, consult a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.

The Industrial Revolution transformed society in several ways, including:

2. Urbanization: The rise of cities was one of the defining features of the Industrial Revolution, as people moved from rural areas to urban centers in search of work.
3. Increased consumption: The Industrial Revolution led to the mass-production and mass-consumption of goods, which had a profound impact on people's lives and lifestyles.

These changes had far-reaching consequences for society, including the creation of new social classes and the development of new forms of entertainment, education, and culture.

Symptoms of Lip Cancer:

1. Ulcer in the mouth or on the lip that won't heal
2. Constant pain or soreness
3. Red or white patches in the mouth
4. Lump on the lip, tongue, or in the neck
5. Bad breath
6. Unexplained bleeding in the mouth
7. Numbness in the mouth

Treatment Options:

The most common treatment for lip cancer is surgery, specifically Mohs surgery, which offers the highest cure rate of any treatment modality for primary or recurrent lip tumors. This involves removing the cancerous cells and some surrounding healthy tissue until no more cancer is found. If the cancer has spread to the lymph nodes, additional treatments such as radiation therapy may be necessary.

Symptoms of lip cancer resemble those of other conditions, so seeking medical attention is essential if any of these symptoms persist or worsen over time.

Quartiles are three points in a data set that divide it into four equal groups, each representing a quarter of the data. The first quartile, also known as the 25th percentile or Q1, splits the lower 25% of data and is the middle value of the lower half. The second quartile, also known as the 50th percentile or Q2, is the median and splits the entire data set in half. The third quartile, also known as the 75th percentile or Q3, splits the lowest 75% or the highest 25% of data. The difference between the first and third quartile is the Interquartile range. Data must be arranged in ascending order for this analysis.

Global egalitarianism is a concept of global justice that emphasizes the importance of equality among individuals and groups worldwide. This perspective holds that global justice requires all individuals to have equal access to resources and opportunities, regardless of their cultural background or location.

The first passage highlights the limitations of global egalitarianism by arguing that measuring the resources or opportunities available to people in different societies in a culturally neutral way is impossible. Therefore, the principle of global justice cannot be based solely on equality of resources or equality of opportunity.

The second passage states that the world is highly unequal in socio-economic terms, with certain individuals and groups having more wealth and opportunities than others. This inequality presents a major challenge to global justice.

The third passage distinguishes between instrumental and non-instrumental forms of egalitarianism. Instrumental egalitarianism seeks to promote equality as a means to achieve some other goal, while non-instrumental egalitarianism values equality for its own sake or as partially constituting some other end.

Global egalitarianism is therefore a conception of global justice that prioritizes equality among individuals and groups worldwide while recognizing the challenges involved in measuring and achieving equality in a global context.

The brewing process starts with malting, where the grain is soaked in water for around 40 hours. Then, the grain is milled or crushed into a coarse flour called grist. The grist is mixed with hot water in a large vessel called a mash tun to create a sugar-rich liquid called wort. The wort is separated from the solids through lautering, which involves sparging the grains with hot water to extract as much sugar as possible.

The liquid wort is then boiled in a large kettle or brew pot, where hops are added to give the beer its bitterness, flavor, and aroma. After the boil, the wort is cooled and transferred to a fermentation vessel, where yeast is added to convert the sugars into alcohol through fermentation.

Once fermentation is complete, the beer is racked, or transferred, to a secondary fermentation vessel, where it ages and develops its flavors. Finally, the beer is packaged, either bottled or kegged, and ready for consumption.

Its amenities include street parking, free WiFi, outdoor seating, and accommodation for groups. It does not offer reservations or valet parking. Its overall rating is 4 stars. Reviews highlight tasty food, good drinks, and friendly service, despite a lack of traditional hosting. One reviewer describes the establishment as more bar-like than a restaurant, and another says it felt like being in a cute Havana restaurant. The restaurant also offers takeout.

Cajun Kitchen is a restaurant located at 420 S Fairview Ave in Goleta, California. It specializes in Cajun/Creole cuisine and is classified under the Restaurants category. The business has outdoor seating and offers takeout options. Customers have rated the business with an average of 3.5 out of 5 stars.

The jambalaya served at Cajun Kitchen is particularly popular and well-regarded by customers. Some customers have noted that the shrimp in the dish is not fresh, but the overall flavor and quality are still appreciated. The corn bread and eggs over easy are also highly praised.

Service at the restaurant is friendly and efficient, with customers appreciating the promptness and politeness of the staff. Some customers have also commented on the availability of soju, which adds to the dining experience. Overall, customers enjoy their experience at Cajun Kitchen and appreciate the unique atmosphere and menu offerings.

GoToCafe is a food and cafe located in Goleta, California. They offer a wide range of options, including American, New and Mexican cuisine. They provide services like food delivery, restaurants and good for groups. They have outdoor seating and free Wi-Fi. Their business hours are Monday through Friday from 8 am to 2:30 pm. Customers appreciate the variety and quality of food offered at GoToCafe. The staff is also very friendly and helpful. The breakfast burritos are a standout dish at the cafe. GoToCafe is a great place for breakfast, lunch or a snack.

Pro Karaoke System Rentals is a local business in Santa Barbara, CA that specializes in karaoke system rentals for parties and events. Customers have given the business positive reviews, praising the owner, Mike, for his excellent service and friendly demeanor. Customers describe Mike as service-oriented and value his great advice, which makes the rental process simple and enjoyable. The speakers provided by Pro Karaoke System Rentals deliver great sound quality.

Customers also appreciate the convenience and user-friendliness of the karaoke system. It comes with a couple of microphones, songbooks, and a signup sheet, making it easy for customers to host their own karaoke party. Users can change the key of the song and adjust the volume of both the music and the singer. The song selection is extensive and varied, and a downloadable PDF songbook makes searching easy.

Customers recommend Pro Karaoke System Rentals for its instant party entertainment and the ease of the whole experience. The owner provides personalized instructions, delivers the system, and walks customers through the setup process. The karaoke machine is always up to date with the latest hit songs, adding to the fun of the party. Pro Karaoke System Rentals is a highly recommended and affordable option for hosting karaoke events in Santa Barbara.

The Bourbon Room is a local business located at 4444 Hollister Ave, Santa Barbara, CA. It operates from 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM Monday through Thursday and until 10:30 PM on Fridays and Saturdays. The restaurant serves American (New) cuisine, including pizzas and burgers, offers outdoor seating and takeout, and accommodates group dining. It does not offer WiFi and has a casual, hipster ambience. The Bourbon Room provides lot parking but does not have valet service.

The restaurant has an average rating of 4 stars. Customer reviews highlight its friendly service, good food, and great drinks. Some customers describe the food as decent but expensive and the parking lot as tight. Customers recommend visiting during happy hour and making reservations in advance due to its popularity. Recommended dishes include the bacon-wrapped dates, Kai's Pizza, and the Manhattan cocktail.

Ridley-Tree House Restaurant, located at 500 Ninos Dr, Santa Barbara, CA, is a fast food restaurant known for its quality burgers and fries in customer reviews. It operates every day from 10:00 to 17:00. The restaurant offers outdoor seating but provides no information about business parking, Wi-Fi, reservations, take out options, or suitability for groups. The ambiance is not classified as touristy, hipster, romantic, divey, intimate, trendy, upscale, classy, or casual. The restaurant has an overall rating of 3 stars. Customer reviews vary: two customers praised the quality of the food and easy online ordering system, while one customer expressed dissatisfaction with the service, stating that the staff insisted on online orders, which was inconvenient for them.

Thario's Kitchen is a local restaurant at 3807 Santa Claus Ln in Carpinteria, CA, specializing in pizza and Italian cuisine. Its 4.5-star rating reflects customers’ high regard for the restaurant. Free WiFi and outdoor seating provide a comfortable setting for customers to enjoy their meals.

Thario's Kitchen serves a diverse menu that includes chicken piccata, bruschetta, and pizza. Customers praise the food’s quality and taste, highlighting the tender chicken in the chicken piccata and the flavorful pizza toppings. Fresh bread and olives are served as complimentary starters.

The restaurant has a welcoming, friendly atmosphere, prompt service, and a selection of nice wines. Customers describe it as a special place that evokes memories and makes them feel comfortable. Its ambience is casual, classy, and romantic. The restaurant also offers takeout and accommodates groups.

Thario's Kitchen is recommended for its delicious food, great service, and pleasant dining experience. It is a popular choice for locals and visitors passing through Santa Claus Lane.

IHOP is a casual dining restaurant located at 1701 State St, Santa Barbara, CA. The restaurant categorizes itself under Breakfast & Brunch, American (Traditional), and Burgers. Its operating hours vary throughout the week, and it is closed on Mondays. The restaurant offers free WiFi and outdoor seating. It is well-equipped for groups and offers take-out options. It does not take reservations. A parking lot is available, but there is no garage, street, validated, or valet parking. The business has an overall star rating of 3.0. Customer reviews highlight the friendly and attentive staff, consistency in food and service, and a wide variety of menu items that cater to the whole family. Some customers have expressed concerns about long wait times.

Rebar Coffee + Ktchn is a local business located at 214 State St in Santa Barbara, CA. The establishment offers a variety of services including coffee and tea, deli options, bakery items, and a restaurant. The business operates from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm from Monday to Saturday, and from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm on Sundays. The business provides free WiFi and outdoor seating for customers. Takeout options are also available for those who prefer to enjoy their food and drinks elsewhere. The business has a rating of 4.0 stars.

Customer reviews of Rebar Coffee + Ktchn are mixed. One customer expressed disappointment with the business's focus on aesthetics rather than addressing important issues like sustainability and climate change. Another customer found the coffee place cute and the staff friendly. The availability of snacks and the appealing outdoor patio area were also appreciated. A negative review mentioned poor customer service, specifically regarding a staff member named Kylie C. Rebar Coffee + Ktchn offers a range of food and drink options with a pleasant outdoor seating area, but improvements in certain areas, such as sustainability and customer service, will enhance the overall experience for customers.

Mama Lu is an Asian Fusion, Chinese restaurant located at 415 N Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA. The restaurant offers take-out and accommodates groups, but it does not offer WiFi, outdoor seating, or reservations. The restaurant’s ambiance is undistinctive, and the establishment is known for its business parking lot. Its overall customer review rating is 3 stars. One customer praised the a la carte options, quick serving time, and respectful staff. Other customers criticized the food’s quality and taste, particularly the buffet, describing it as dry, flavorless, and substandard compared to other Chinese restaurants. The second reviewer also reported poor service initially but noted that the restaurant was clean and neat.

Mercury Lounge, located at 5871 Hollister Ave in Goleta, CA, is a popular locale for music, arts, entertainment, and nightlife. With an average business rating of 4.0 stars, the venue offers a multitude of activities, including trivia nights, live bands, and movie nights, along with a robust selection of beers. The lounge features a diverse ambiance with a casual, classy, and slightly divey feel. It also offers outdoor seating and is suitable for groups. Despite claims of non-compliance with mask mandates and unfair treatment of customers, many other customers laud the venue for its welcoming atmosphere and commend the staff. Mercury Lounge operates Thursdays to Saturdays from late afternoon to late evening. It offers street and lot parking but does not have WiFi.

Stearns Wharf is a popular local business located at 217 Stearns Wharf in Santa Barbara, California. It is a landmark and historical building that offers a range of services and activities to visitors. The business is categorized under Public Services & Government, Landmarks & Historical Buildings, Local Flavor, Restaurants, Tours, Shopping, Shopping Centers, Seafood, Hotels & Travel, and Boat Tours.

The wharf is known for its scenic ocean views, making it a perfect place for a leisurely walk. It also houses various restaurants and gift shops, providing visitors with dining and shopping options. Parking is not free, but many customers find it worth paying for the chance to enjoy Santa Barbara's picturesque surroundings.

One unique aspect of Stearns Wharf is that it allows visitors to drive onto it, unlike many other wharfs in the Pacific Northwest. This feature adds to its charm and makes it a notable attraction for tourists. Fishing is permitted at the end of the wharf, where crab traps and fishing activities provide enjoyment, especially for children.

The wharf dates back to 1872, making it the oldest working wharf in California. Its wide structure and wooden construction create a unique experience, although some visitors describe driving on it as feeling like riding a slow-motion wooden rollercoaster.

Free public bathrooms are available for visitors' convenience. Additionally, the wharf offers a psychic/fortune teller service, although it was closed during the visit of one customer.

Stearns Wharf is a highly visited destination in Santa Barbara, offering a mix of historical significance, scenic views, dining options, and shopping opportunities.

Rudy's is a Mexican restaurant located at 138 E Canon Perdido St in Santa Barbara, CA. The restaurant is known for its quick service and delicious food, particularly its crunchy chicken tacos generously filled with chicken and lettuce. Customers highly recommend Rudy's for good food that always hits the spot.

The restaurant operates from 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM every day of the week. It offers free WiFi for customers and takeout options. Rudy's also accommodates group dining in a casual and trendy ambience.

Rudy's has an average customer rating of 4.0 stars. One customer stated that their wife loves the tacos at Rudy's and considers them the best in Santa Barbara. Another customer has been a loyal patron of Rudy's for almost 10 years and appreciates the combination burrito, especially when served wet.

One negative review described a customer accidentally receiving non-vegan food instead of the vegan burrito they had ordered. This caused the customer to vomit in their car. Despite this incident, the customer received a refund.

Rudy's is a popular local Mexican restaurant in Santa Barbara, known for its quick service, delicious food, and positive dining experiences.

Petrini's Italian Restaurant is located at 14 W Calle Laureles in Santa Barbara, California. It serves pizza, pasta, and Italian cuisine, and is open seven days a week from 4:30 PM to 8:00 PM. The restaurant offers outdoor seating and takes out orders, making it a great option for groups or people who don't have time to sit down.

The restaurant has received mixed reviews, with some customers praising the service and the quality of the food, while others have had negative experiences with overcooked and poorly prepared dishes. Overall, customers enjoy the casual atmosphere of the restaurant, with many commenting on its affordable prices. Petrini's Italian Restaurant is a good choice for a quick and affordable meal. However, other options are preferable for a more high-end dining experience.

Coast Restaurant & Bar is a local business located at Canary Hotel, 31 W Carrillo St, in Santa Barbara, CA. It offers a variety of services, including restaurants, event planning & services, and American cuisine. The restaurant is open from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM Monday through Thursday, and until 11:00 PM on Fridays and Saturdays. On Sundays, it operates from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

The restaurant has received mixed customer feedback. One customer praised the lounge setting and ambiance as wonderful and relaxing. They enjoyed the warm and tasty bread, butternut squash soup, and romaine wedge salad. However, they said the main course, including the short ribs and New York steak, lacked flavor. The dessert, consisting of butterscotch pudding and lemon cheesecake, received high praise.

Another customer had a positive experience and highlighted the restaurant's convenient location in their hotel's lobby. They enjoyed roasted California mussels, Manilla clams, crispy duck breast, and bread pudding. They described the service as friendly and quick.

A third customer appreciated the variety of dishes they tried, particularly the mussels and accompanying sourdough toast. They also spoke with the head chef, James Siao, who received positive feedback.

Coast Restaurant & Bar offers a pleasant ambiance and a diverse menu. Some customers found the main dishes lacking in flavor, while others had a delightful dining experience.

Domino's Pizza at 617 N Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA is a popular spot for pizza lovers. They offer a wide variety of pizzas, sandwiches, and chicken wings. The restaurant is open seven days a week from 10:30 am to midnight, except on Fridays and Saturdays, when they close at 1 am. They also offer takeout and delivery services. Customer reviews raise concerns about the quality of their service and food. Some customers have reported long wait times, unhelpful staff, and poorly cooked food. Complaints also address the cleanliness of the store and the behavior of some employees. Despite these issues, the restaurant maintains an average rating of 1.5 stars out of 5.

The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf in Santa Barbara, CA is a popular restaurant with 3.5 stars out of 5. The establishment has a cozy atmosphere with outdoor seating and offers free WiFi. The menu includes a variety of coffee and tea drinks, as well as food items like pastries and sandwiches. One customer praised the use of paper straws and the upfront nutrition information for drinks, while another reviewer appreciated the friendly service and rich Vietnamese cold brew. However, one customer had a negative experience with an employee asking to see a receipt before filling their cup, which was awkward and environmentally insensitive. Overall, The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf is a good spot for coffee and tea lovers, with a focus on sustainability and friendly service.

Tepeyac Taquitos is a Mexican restaurant located at 201 W Carrillo St in Santa Barbara, CA. The restaurant has an overall rating of 3.5 stars. Customers have praised its taquitos, with one customer stating that they were pleasantly surprised by their quality, as they initially did not associate Santa Barbara with this type of cuisine. That customer specifically recommends the Surtido #1, which includes one of each of the taquitos on the menu, along with lettuce, tomato, onion, sour cream, and guacamole. The owners are fun to talk with and down to earth. The price for the taquitos and a drink is just under $10. Another customer reported a great experience at Tepeyac Taquitos, particularly enjoying the vegetarian options available. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable, and the owners are super friendly. One review stated that the restaurant is currently closed.
